title: Looking for People Who May Not Be Found: Relative Clauses

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *Busco un apartamento que tenga balcón* from B2 Unit 13: a relative clause with *que* takes the subjunctive when you cannot point at the person or thing: you are looking for it, you do not know if it exists, or it does not exist. The search of the Abuelas de Plaza de Mayo is exactly that: they look for grandchildren who do not yet know who they are.

sections.title: Subjunctive or indicative after que?
rows: Las Abuelas buscan a nietos que no conozcan su origen.
subjunctive: they do not know who or where those grandchildren are
Las Abuelas conocen a un joven que recuperó su identidad.
indicative: a real person they can name
Piden a las personas que tengan dudas que se acerquen.
subjunctive: anyone who might have doubts
No hay ningún documento que diga dónde está el niño.

items.spanish: Las Abuelas buscan a nietos que no conozcan su origen.
items.english: The Abuelas look for grandchildren who may not know their origin.

items.spanish: Las Abuelas conocen a un joven que recuperó su identidad.
items.english: The Abuelas know a young man who recovered his identity.

items.spanish: Piden a las personas que tengan dudas que se acerquen.
items.english: They ask people who have doubts to come forward.

items.spanish: No hay ningún documento que diga dónde está el niño.
items.english: There is no document that says where the child is.

sections.content: Ask yourself: can I point at it? If yes, the indicative (*un joven que recuperó*). If you are only looking for it, it may not exist or it does not exist, the subjunctive (*que no conozcan*, *que diga*). Keep the personal *a* before people: *buscan a nietos que…*.
